findings.evidence: Static control-flow finding, not an observed production failure: terminate() guards both kill(-pgid) and destroyForcibly() with process.isAlive. If the Python group leader exits or is killed independently while FFmpeg/another helper remains in its already-established process group, isAlive is false, so cancel()/finally never signal the surviving group; execute() then deletes the only PGID record. The current real cancellation test leaves the parent sleeping for120s and cancels while it is alive, so it cannot detect this case. A surviving helper can keep consuming CPU/storage or retain a pipe after its owning task has ended.
findings.recommendation: Track ownership of the established process group independently from leader liveness and reap/terminate that owned group during all terminal paths, with an explicit PID/group-reuse safeguard. Add a controlled native fixture whose leader spawns a sleeping helper, records its PID, exits immediately (or is killed), then assert helper termination, bounded execute/cancel completion and PID-record cleanup. Do not simply send an unverified stale PGID after arbitrary delay.

test_gaps: No native regression for an exited group leader with a surviving helper; this is the prerequisite to verify/fix finding01.

No forced cold-initialization cancellation/retry fixture spanning YoutubeDL.init, shared-file installation and FFmpeg.init. Ready is correctly set only at successful completion, but the wrapper singleton and partial state should be exercised together.

MediaEngine session admission is a volatile check-then-set at lines31-32, not atomic. Existing inspected callers serialize admission on Main; no current user-facing race was proven. Add atomic admission or an explicit single-thread contract before implementing multiple-active-download execution.

The PGID record is stored in cacheDir; loss of that record while helpers run currently falls back to killing only the leader. Storage-pressure/record-loss behavior needs a fixture or an ownership record retained independently from evictable cache.
positive_observations: ProcessLease cancellation is sticky across the start-before-registration window; the two-thread200-round test covers that invariant.
Per-invocation UUID, structured argv, authenticated per-session proxy and a suspended cancellation guard avoid a shared process map and permanent polling worker.
EngineRuntime initialization is synchronized and marks ready only after all initializers succeed; cancellation before process execution remains checked by the session lease.
runtime_execution: No emulator/native fixture was started by this reviewer. Conclusions distinguish source-proven conditional behavior from missing device evidence.

mechanism: Per-session in-memory HMAC key authenticates bootstrap PID/starttime/UUID record; the key is removed from the inherited environment before loading yt-dlp.
Original live/unreaped leader ownership is checked using authenticated starttime, UID, PGID and SID without requiring environ access.
When the leader has disappeared, a bounded lazy /proc scan requires the inherited session UUID on a member of that exact PGID/SID with a compatible starttime.
A short cross-process fcntl/FileChannel lock in noBackupFilesDir serializes all NativeProcessSession setsid creation against identity verification and group signaling.
UI-thread cancellation dispatches cleanup to existing Dispatchers.IO; no dedicated monitoring process/thread was introduced.
Nonblocking tryLock retries on IO are limited to2s; /proc enumeration is limited to200ms/2048 entries. An unverified or unavailable identity never authorizes a numeric PGID signal.
verification_done: Python bootstrap and all embedded fixtures parsed using ast.parse
remaining_limits: If Android denies helper environ access after the leader is gone, group cleanup fails closed, retains its record and records native_cleanup_unverified.
The creation gate coordinates all current NativeProcessSession groups, not unrelated/future code creating process groups outside that protocol.
Prolonged gate contention or proof/scan budget exhaustion can leave a helper; the owned Process is stopped but no unverified group is killed.
The PGID metadata remains in cacheDir; cache eviction while helpers survive is still a fail-closed limitation. The protocol lock itself is in noBackupFilesDir.
